title: Bug: Synchronous `subprocess.run` inside `_NodeComponentRuntime` blocks the event loop
body:
In `pyxle/ssr/renderer.py`, the `_NodeComponentRuntime` (which acts as the fallback renderer when the worker pool is unavailable or disabled) uses `subprocess.run` to execute Node.js SSR rendering. 

```python
            process = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - controlled command invocation
                command,
                ...
            )
```

Because `_NodeComponentRuntime.render` is called in the context of handling an async request in Starlette, executing a synchronous, blocking `subprocess.run` directly will block the main ASGI event loop. This leads to starvation and degraded performance when handling concurrent requests (violating the project convention that all I/O operations must be async and non-blocking). 

**Recommendation:**
Wrap the `subprocess.run` invocation with `asyncio.to_thread()` so the blocking operation executes in a separate thread, keeping the event loop responsive.
